Alex,

Appreciate the clear list — see initial responses below and attached a concise pack (redwood_sig_responses_20261129.pdf) with excerpts from our control docs. Naomi and Dylan are copied for technical attachments and rotation logs — Naomi will push the logs in a follow-up.

Short answers:
- In transit: TLS 1.2+ (mutual TLS available for Dedicated/Private); all hosted API traffic is terminated on our load balancers and uses TLS in transit by default. No exceptions for customer API traffic.
- At rest: All customer data stored on our platform is encrypted at rest by default using per-customer DEKs protected by a master KEK.
- Hybrid KMS/HSM model: We use a cloud KMS for key management operations and an HSM-backed root for KEK wrapping for hosted environments. HSM is used for wrapping/unwrapping the KEK material and signing root-level key attestations. Data keys are generated per-customer and are encrypted (wrapped) with the KEK.
- Rotation: KEK rotation is configured as a managed process. Master KEKs rotate annually by default; DEKs rotate on-demand during key rollover events and can be rotated programmatically. We can support a 90-day rotation cadence on request — that requires an operational change and a brief maintenance window (documented in the attached).

We'll attach the rotation logs and a short README with the timestamps and HSM provenance. Expect Naomi's message shortly with the log bundle.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
